title: "TO BE" Verb - Am / Is / Are - Exercise 1

source.translation: Bản dịch tiếng Việt do Lumos thực hiện

cues.en: Hi, and welcome back for more learning through exercises.
For this exercise, we are going to fill in the blanks with the appropriate form of the verb 'to be' (am, is, are). Let's begin!
Tom is a carpenter.
We use "is", as the verb "to be" for "Tom", which is a singular third person.
Terry and Linda are from Armenia. We use "are", as the verb "to be" for Terry and Linda, because they are two people.
Jack is a famous movie star. "Jack" is singular, so we use "is".
Are Derek and Peter police officers? We use "Are", to form a question in the present tense for plural subjects (Derek and Peter).
BMW is an expensive car brand.
"Is", is used to indicate the singular nature of the car brand.
Alan's friends are doctors. We use "are", for Alan's friends, which is plural.
We are at home. We use are, for the plural "We".
I am a diligent student.
We use 'am', as the verb "to be", for the singular first person.
They are my friend's cousins. We use "are", because, "they" is plural!
Mr. Jackson is a pianist.
We use "is", for the singular third-person Mr. Jackson.
Daniel and Ryan are mechanical engineers. Daniel and Ryan are two people so we use "are".
Are they soldiers? "Soldiers" is plural, so we use "are" to form a question.
His shoes are new. "Shoes", is plural, so we use "are".
Are you the boss?
'Are', to form a question in the present tense for the second-person singular "you".
Is Judy the judge?
'Is', to form a question in the present tense for the third-person "Judy".
Am I the only one here?
Forming a question with "am" in the present tense for the first-person singular subject.
The children are playing.
'Children' is the plural of 'child', so we use the plural form of the verb "to be".
That's all for this exercise, thanks for watching! If you've enjoyed this video,
please hit the like button and consider subscribing to our channel for more content like this! Goodbye, and see you next time!
